title: Declare minimum runtime assurances and gradual pin process for experimental open-models
creator: Arielle Summers
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a concise intake contract and acceptance matrix for new open-source model submissions (community weights) that are flagged as experimental or unpinned. The goal is to reduce friction for contributors while protecting production stability for Redwood customers. We need a short, implementable policy that the Catalog intake flow and the runtime onboarding pipeline can enforce: an explicit set of minimum runtime assurances (performance/regression guardrails), a graduated "soft-pin" process that moves an experimental variant to a pinned/verified state after telemetry, and clear rollback criteria and owners for variants that destabilize downstream serving.

Background / Motivation:
- We are seeing faster model variant submissions from community and partners; many are useful but exhibit subtle runtime incompatibilities (tokenization mismatches, KV cache layout differences, unsupported quantization formats) that cause production regressions.
- The current intake checklist is heavy-weight for small experimental weights and lacks a short contract that runtime and serving engineers can automatically validate.
- Product needs clear acceptance criteria to sign off a catalog entry and to define how and when to pin a variant or rollback.

Goals:
- Define a minimal, machine-checkable "runtime assurances" checklist for experimental model variants.
- Specify a "soft-pin" process: staged exposure, telemetry gates, and automated promotion to pinned status after verification.
- Define rollback triggers, observability signals required to make an automated/ops-assisted rollback decision, and owner responsibilities.
- Ensure compatibility notes surface in the catalog entry and the Console with clear guidance for SDKs and Dedicated customers.

Scope (in):
- New open/community model variants submitted via the catalog intake form that are marked "experimental" or left unpinned.
- Runtime assurance checks executed by onboarding CI and runtime profiling job (latency/memory/kv-cache verification).
- Documentation updates to the Catalog entry template and Console listing (compatibility notes).

Out of scope:
- Rewriting the entire onboarding flow for fully-verified enterprise model subscriptions.
- Major runtime rewrites; this ticket defines gating criteria and process only.

Proposed minimal runtime assurances (intake contract):
1) Tokenization sanity: sample tokenization of standard prompt set (provided by PM) must round-trip (no unsupported tokens).
2) Memory/footprint fingerprint: model load in reference config (X GPU/worker) must not exceed 1.5x baseline for that family.
3) Latency baseline: p95 per-token generation for 256 tokens within X ms (profile job to compute X per family).
4) KV cache compatibility: KV cache indexing must match our expected layout or declare incompatibility as a documented note.
5) Quantization compatibility: if community weights use a quantized file, specify format and declare whether loader is supported.
6) Small eval: top-line quality signals (perplexity or eval harness) against our reference prompt set with a minimum pass threshold or an explicit trade-off note.

Soft-pin process (staged exposure):
- Phase 0 (Intake / Experimental listing): model appears in Catalog as "experimental" with compatibility notes and a soft-pin expiry window (e.g., 30 days). Limited default serving: redwood-hosted routes disabled; allowed in Dedicated when customer opts-in.
- Phase 1 (Canary): limited traffic inside Redwood tests and opt-in customers, telemetry collection enabled, automated anomaly detectors run (latency, error rate, OOMs, perf regressions).
- Phase 2 (Promotion to pinned): if telemetry gates pass for N days (configurable; default 7) without regressions, model moved to pinned status and eligible for broader routing.
- Phase 3 (Rollback / Deprecation): If a regression is detected post-promotion, rollback to last compatible variant and mark the model as "needs attention" until a steward resolves.

Telemetry gates and metrics (minimum):
- Error rate: crash/serve-error increase > 0.5% absolute vs baseline triggers investigation.
- Latency: p50/p95 increase > 20% vs baseline triggers canary rollback.
- Resource OOMs: any OOM or unrecoverable worker crash triggers immediate removal from routing.
- Quality regressions: sampled eval set shows > 15% drop on key quality metric for two consecutive days.

Owners and responsibilities:
- Catalog PM (owner): final sign-off for promotion and for communicating compatibility notes.
- Runtime/Serving ENG: implement the machine-checkable intake jobs and anomaly detectors; own remediation rollouts.
- Model steward (contributor or Redwood E2E steward): resolve incompatibilities and coordinate fixes.

Rollout plan:
1. Publish intake contract template and update intake UI with explicit checkboxes for the six runtime assurances. (PM + Docs)
2. Implement profiling CI job that runs tokenization/memory/latency checks on submit. (ENG)
3. Add soft-pin lifecycle flags and telemetry gates to the Catalog service and Console. (ENG + PM)
4. Run a pilot with three experimental community models and collect operator feedback. (PM + Eng)

Risks & mitigation:
- False negatives/positives in telemetry: start conservative thresholds and iterate with pilot.
- Contributor friction: provide clear guidance and a compatibility checklist generator to make passing checks easier.

Success metrics:
- Reduction in post-onboarding runtime incidents attributable to community variants by 60% in first quarter after rollout.
- Time-to-promotion for experimental variants median < 14 days (from intake to pinned).

Links / artifacts:
- Intake PRD draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Model+Catalog+Intake+Contract
- Profiling CI spike: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding-profiling/pull/58
- Pilot candidate list (internal spreadsheet): https://drive.redwood.com/sheets/pilot-models-2026
acceptance_criteria: Intake UI exposes the six runtime assurances as required fields for experimental submissions and stores the results in the Catalog record.
Onboarding CI job runs tokenization, memory, and latency profiles and posts standardized artifacts (JSON) to the model record on submit.
Console displays 'experimental' soft-pin state with compatibility notes and the soft-pin expiry date for listed models.
Telemetry gates implemented: error rate, latency, OOM, and sampled quality signals produce actionable alerts and an automated flag that excludes model from routing when triggered.
Pilot with at least three community model submissions completed and engineering/PM retrospective documented with recommended threshold adjustments.
A rollback runbook exists and is linked from the Catalog model page for maintainers and SREs.
Security review completed for the intake CI artifacts and compatibility annotations (security_review_required = true).
